chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

If you reach the Imam while he has bowed, and you say the takbir before the Imam raises his head, then you have caught the rakʿah. But if he raises his head before you bow, then that rakʿah has passed you by.

key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.رَأْسَهُ: his head, referring to the Imam rising from bowing
key_terms.رَكَعَ: entered the state of rukuʿ, the bowing posture in prayer
key_terms.فَكَبَّرْتَ: you pronounced the takbir to enter the prayer

ai.seo_question: When do you count a rakʿah if you join the Imam during rukuʿ in congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for congregational salat regarding catching a rakʿah with the Imam in rukuʿ. It teaches that the worshipper counts the rakʿah if he joins and pronounces takbir before the Imam rises from bowing; otherwise, that rakʿah is missed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1150 - Al-Halabi narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:

"If you reach the Imam while he is in the bowing position (ruku') and you say the takbir (opening supplication) before the Imam raises his head, then you have caught the rak'ah (unit of prayer). However, if he raises his head before you bow, then you have missed that rak'ah."
